statement.p: Find the area of the region enclosed by the parametric equation

static.solution:
t = \sqrt {5} and t = -\sqrt {5} yields the same x and y coordinates, namely (0,30). These two values of t are going to be the upper and lower limits of integration.
The area under a curve defined by parameters x = f(t) and y = g(t) can be expressed A = \int ydx =\int g(t)f'(t)dt Plugging in the functions and the upper and lower limits of integration, we have A = \int_{-\sqrt{5}}^{\sqrt{5}} 6 t^2 (3 t^2 - 5) dt = (2) (6) \int_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} (3 t^4 - 5 t^2) dt = 12 \left[ \frac {3}{5} t^5 - \frac {5}{3} t^3 \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{5}} = 12 \left[ \frac {3}{5} 5^{5/2} - \frac {5}{3} 5^{3/2} \right] = 178.885438199983
